summary.headline: Datamatics Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11.5% YoY to INR 546.6 crore, with EBITDA margin up 301 bps to 21.1%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 11.5% YoY to INR 546.6 crore and EBITDA rose 30% to INR 115.5 crore, with margin at 21.1%. Digital Operations led growth at 15.6% with a 21.8% EBIT margin, while Digital Technologies grew 8.8% at a 9.5% margin and Digital Experiences was flat at 0.8%. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 1,060.6 crore (up 10.7%) and PAT after minority interest rose 28.3% to INR 145.8 crore. Net cash and investments fell to INR 557 crore from INR 710.2 crore after the final TNQTech acquisition payment.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBIT (Q2 FY27, excl. TNQTech PPA amortisation)

financial_highlights.value: INR 145.8 crore; EPS INR 24.66; PAT margin 13.4%

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments net of debt
financial_highlights.change: down from INR 710.2 crore at 30 Jun 2026; reflects final TNQTech tranche payment

segments.name: Digital Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 314.9 crore, up 15.6% YoY, with EBIT margin of 21.8%; management credited operating leverage and TNQ growth, and added agentic claims management to the TruAI underwriting offering in insurance.

segments.name: Digital Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 166.6 crore, up 8.8% YoY, with EBIT margin of 9.5%; R&D costs (about INR 40-50 crore) are booked in this segment and hardware costs weighed on the Fare Collection business.

segments.name: Digital Experiences
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 65.1 crore, up 0.8% YoY, with EBIT margin of 12%; management described the business as stable.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: US 57% of business, UK and Europe 24%, India 12%, RoW 7%; US and Europe were the primary growth drivers.

segments.name: Client concentration
segments.commentary: Top 5, 10 and 20 clients contributed 29%, 39% and 53% of revenue; top 5 was 26% in Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at high single digits; management now expects about 9-9.5% versus earlier 7.5-8%, with H1 at 10.7%.
EBITDA margin expected to hold around 20%; the 100-150 bps improvement targeted at the start of the year is being achieved, and management expects H2 to remain steady.
Medium-term target of INR 3,000 crore revenue in 3 years, implying about 15% CAGR: roughly 10-12% organic and 3-4% inorganic.
Headcount expected to stay roughly flat, with a possible marginal increase, from about 14,000-15,000 people, as AI tools absorb growth.
FY28 planning to be discussed at Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Net cash and investments of INR 557 crore are available for acquisitions; management said nothing has matured yet but it is in dialogue with several companies.
TNQTech purchase-price-allocation intangibles amortise over 12 quarters from Q4 FY25 and will be fully amortised by Q3 FY28; this non-cash charge is excluded from adjusted EBIT.
KAi Modernization Factory cited as delivering up to 40% cost savings and 3x faster go-live.
demand_pricing: About 55% of current opportunities are heavily AI-driven; management does not disclose revenue from TruAI, TruBot, TruCap+ or other platforms because they are bundled with services.
Client additions slowed to about 6-7 in H1 FY27 from 15-18 per quarter earlier, as the strategy shifted to account mining and selective hunting within the ICP.
Top-50 accounts are the focus for growth; management said the decline in top-5/top-10 share in some quarters was due to non-top accounts growing, not GCC insourcing.
Revenue models are T&M, outcome-based and fixed price; Digital Operations is largely outcome-based. Management did not give a split.
Annual wage hike was applied effective 1 April 2026 (Q1 FY27), with a partial hike in October and April.

qa_highlights.question: What organic and inorganic growth is needed to reach INR 3,000 crore revenue in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 15% CAGR, of which 10-12% is organic and 3-4% inorganic; no acquisition has matured yet, though talks are under way.

qa_highlights.question: How much AI monetisation is there, and is the 21.1% EBITDA margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: AI platform revenue is not disclosed because it is bundled into services; about 55% of opportunities are heavily AI-driven. Management said the margin is fairly sustainable and H2 should remain steady near 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Digital Operations margin, and what were the currency and TNQ effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency was steady quarter on quarter, so margin gains came from growth and operating leverage; TNQ also grew well, and no digital content/finance split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Digital Technologies margin low?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly hardware cost pressure in the Fare Collection business, and mainly R&D costs (about INR 40-50 crore) booked in the technology segment, which supports all units.

qa_highlights.question: Is customer concentration falling because of GCC insourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied GCC insourcing; the change reflects growth in non-top-5 and non-top-10 accounts from the account-mining strategy. Top 20 rose to 53%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the headcount trajectory for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is expected to stay roughly flat or rise marginally from about 14,000-15,000 as AI tools absorb growth; the figure could reach about 15,500.

risks_watch: Digital Technologies margin at 9.5% and hardware cost pressure on Fare Collection.
Slower new-logo additions (6-7 in H1 vs 15-18 per quarter previously) could limit growth beyond existing accounts.
Pace of acquisitions needed for the INR 3,000 crore target; the 3-4% inorganic component is not yet tied to a deal.
DSO of 66 days and falling cash balance after the TNQTech payment.
Revenue model mix (outcome-based share) was not quantified, and management promised to follow up.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and H2 outlook, with management saying H1 beat its expectations. Vague on specifics: it declined to quantify AI platform revenue, the revenue-model split and the Digital Operations sub-segment split.
key_quotes: Datamatics delivered another strong quarter with healthy revenue growth and margin expansion.
So that strategy has been implemented. We are focusing on farming and mining existing accounts and those relationships are panning out quite well.
So the headcount, we don't expect headcount to increase in proportion to revenue largely because we are using more and more AI tools, and we see that happening.
